1 The Roman Pontiff claims for himself [in the first place] that by divine right he is [supreme] above all bishops and pastors [in all Christendom].

text: 2 Secondly, he adds also that by divine right he has both swords, i.e., the authority also of bestowing kingdoms [enthroning and deposing kings, regulating secular dominions etc.].
text_raw: 2 Secondly, he adds also that by divine right he has both swords, i.e., the authority also of bestowing kingdoms [enthroning and deposing kings, regulating secular dominions etc.].

text: 3 And thirdly, he says that to believe this is necessary for salvation.
text_raw: 3 And thirdly, he says that to believe this is necessary for salvation.

text: And for these reasons the Roman bishop calls himself [and boasts that he is] the vicar of Christ on earth.
text_raw: And for these reasons the Roman bishop calls himself [and boasts that he is] the vicar of Christ on earth.

text: 4 These three articles we hold to be false, godless, tyrannical, and [quite] pernicious to the Church.
text_raw: 4 These three articles we hold to be false, godless, tyrannical, and [quite] pernicious to the Church.

text: 5 Now, in order that our proof [reason and opinion] may be [better] understood, we shall first define what they call being above all [what it means that he boasts of being supreme] by divine right.
text_raw: 5 Now, in order that our proof [reason and opinion] may be [better] understood, we shall first define what they call being above all [what it means that he boasts of being supreme] by divine right.

text: For they mean that he is universal [that the Pope is the general bishop over the entire Christian Church], or, as they say, ecumenical bishop, i.e., from whom all bishops and pastors throughout the entire world ought to seek ordination and [confirmation, who [alone] is to have the right of electing, ordaining, confirming, deposing all bishops [and pastors].
text_raw: For they mean that he is universal [that the Pope is the general bishop over the entire Christian Church], or, as they say, ecumenical bishop, i.e., from whom all bishops and pastors throughout the entire world ought to seek ordination and [confirmation, who [alone] is to have the right of electing, ordaining, confirming, deposing all bishops [and pastors].

text: 6 Besides this, he arrogates to himself the authority to make [all kinds of] laws concerning acts of worship, concerning changing the Sacraments [and] concerning doctrine, and wishes his articles, his decrees, his laws [his statutes and ordinances] to be considered equal to the divine laws [to other articles of the Christian Creed and the Holy Scriptures], i.e., he holds that by the papal laws the consciences of men are so bound that those who neglect them, even without public offense, sin mortally [that they cannot be omitted without sin.
text_raw: 6 Besides this, he arrogates to himself the authority to make [all kinds of] laws concerning acts of worship, concerning changing the Sacraments [and] concerning doctrine, and wishes his articles, his decrees, his laws [his statutes and ordinances] to be considered equal to the divine laws [to other articles of the Christian Creed and the Holy Scriptures], i.e., he holds that by the papal laws the consciences of men are so bound that those who neglect them, even without public offense, sin mortally [that they cannot be omitted without sin.

text: For he wishes to found this power upon divine right and the Holy Scriptures; yea, he wishes to have it preferred to the Holy Scriptures and God’s commands].
text_raw: For he wishes to found this power upon divine right and the Holy Scriptures; yea, he wishes to have it preferred to the Holy Scriptures and God’s commands].

text: And what he adds is still more horrible, namely, that it is necessary to believe all these things in order to be saved [all these things shall and must be believed at the peril of forfeiting salvation].
text_raw: And what he adds is still more horrible, namely, that it is necessary to believe all these things in order to be saved [all these things shall and must be believed at the peril of forfeiting salvation].

text: 7 In the first place, therefore, let us show from the [holy] Gospel that the Roman bishop is not by divine right above [cannot arrogate to himself any supremacy whatever over] other bishops and pastors.
text_raw: 7 In the first place, therefore, let us show from the [holy] Gospel that the Roman bishop is not by divine right above [cannot arrogate to himself any supremacy whatever over] other bishops and pastors.

text: Luke 22:25.

text: Christ expressly prohibits lordship among the apostles [that no apostle should have any supremacy over the rest].
text_raw: Christ expressly prohibits lordship among the apostles [that no apostle should have any supremacy over the rest].

text: For this was the very question, namely, that when Christ spake of His passion, they were disputing who should be at the head, and as it were the vicar of the absent Christ.
text_raw: For this was the very question, namely, that when Christ spake of His passion, they were disputing who should be at the head, and as it were the vicar of the absent Christ.

text: There Christ reproves this error of the apostles and teaches that there shall not be lordship or superiority among them, but that the apostles should be sent forth as equals to the common ministry of the Gospel.
text_raw: There Christ reproves this error of the apostles and teaches that there shall not be lordship or superiority among them, but that the apostles should be sent forth as equals to the common ministry of the Gospel.

text: Accordingly, He says:
text_raw: Accordingly, He says:

text: The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors, but ye shall not be so; but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.

text: The antithesis here shows [By holding these matters against one another, one sees] that lordship [among the apostles] is disapproved.
text_raw: The antithesis here shows [By holding these matters against one another, one sees] that lordship [among the apostles] is disapproved.

text: 2:7f St. Paul manifestly affirms that he was neither ordained nor confirmed [and endorsed] by Peter, nor does he acknowledge Peter to be one from whom confirmation should be sought.

text: And he expressly contends concerning this point that his call does not depend upon the authority of Peter.
text_raw: And he expressly contends concerning this point that his call does not depend upon the authority of Peter.

text: But he ought to have acknowledged Peter as a superior if Peter was superior by divine right [if Peter, indeed, had received such supremacy from Christ].
text_raw: But he ought to have acknowledged Peter as a superior if Peter was superior by divine right [if Peter, indeed, had received such supremacy from Christ].

text: Since Paul, then, clearly testifies that he did not even wish to seek for the confirmation of Peter [for permission to preach] even when he had come to him, he teaches that the authority of the ministry depends upon the Word of God, and that Peter was not superior to the other apostles, and that it was not from this one individual Peter that ordination or confirmation was to be sought [that the office of the ministry proceeds from the general call of the apostles, and that it is not necessary for all to have the call or confirmation of this one person, Peter, alone].

text: 3:6, Paul makes ministers equal, and teaches that the Church is above the ministers.
text_raw: 3:6, Paul makes ministers equal, and teaches that the Church is above the ministers.

text: Hence superiority or lordship over the Church or the rest of the ministers is not ascribed to Peter [in preference to other apostles].
text_raw: Hence superiority or lordship over the Church or the rest of the ministers is not ascribed to Peter [in preference to other apostles].

text: For he says thus:
text_raw: For he says thus:

text: All things are yours, whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, i.e., let neither the other ministers nor Peter assume for themselves lordship or superiority over the Church; let them not burden the Church with traditions; let not the authority of any avail more than the Word [of God]; let not the authority of Cephas be opposed to the authority of the other apostles, as they reasoned at that time: “Cephas, who is an apostle of higher rank, observes this; therefore, both Paul and the rest ought to observe this.” Paul removes this pretext from Peter, and denies [Not so, says Paul, and makes Peter doff his little hat, namely, the claim] that his authority is to be preferred to the rest or to the Church.
text_raw: All things are yours, whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, i.e., let neither the other ministers nor Peter assume for themselves lordship or superiority over the Church; let them not burden the Church with traditions; let not the authority of any avail more than the Word [of God]; let not the authority of Cephas be opposed to the authority of the other apostles, as they reasoned at that time: “Cephas, who is an apostle of higher rank, observes this; therefore, both Paul and the rest ought to observe this.” Paul removes this pretext from Peter, and denies [Not so, says Paul, and makes Peter doff his little hat, namely, the claim] that his authority is to be preferred to the rest or to the Church.

text: 12 VI.
text_raw: 12 VI.

text: The Council of Nice resolved that the bishop of Alexandria should administer the churches in the East, and the Roman bishop the suburban, i.e., those which were in the Roman provinces in the West.
text_raw: The Council of Nice resolved that the bishop of Alexandria should administer the churches in the East, and the Roman bishop the suburban, i.e., those which were in the Roman provinces in the West.

text: From this start by a human law, i.e. the resolution of the Council, the authority of the Roman bishop first arose.
text_raw: From this start by a human law, i.e. the resolution of the Council, the authority of the Roman bishop first arose.

text: If the Roman bishop already had the superiority by divine law, it would not have been lawful for the Council to take any right from him and transfer it to the bishop of Alexandria; nay, all the bishops of the East ought perpetually to have sought ordination and confirmation from the bishop of Rome.
text_raw: If the Roman bishop already had the superiority by divine law, it would not have been lawful for the Council to take any right from him and transfer it to the bishop of Alexandria; nay, all the bishops of the East ought perpetually to have sought ordination and confirmation from the bishop of Rome.

text: 13 VII.
text_raw: 13 VII.

text: Again the Council of Nice determined that bishops should be elected by their own churches, in the presence of some neighboring bishop or of several.
text_raw: Again the Council of Nice determined that bishops should be elected by their own churches, in the presence of some neighboring bishop or of several.

text: 14 The same was observed [for a long time, not only in the East, but] also in the West and in the Latin churches, as Cyprian and Augustine testify.
text_raw: 14 The same was observed [for a long time, not only in the East, but] also in the West and in the Latin churches, as Cyprian and Augustine testify.

text: For Cyprian says in his fourth letter to Cornelius:
text_raw: For Cyprian says in his fourth letter to Cornelius:

text: Accordingly, as regards the divine observance and apostolic practice, you must diligently keep and practice what is also observed among us and in almost all the provinces, that for celebrating ordination properly, whatsoever bishops of the same province live nearest should come together with the people for whom a pastor is being appointed, and the bishop should be chosen in the presence of the people, who most fully know the life of each one, which we also have seen done among us at the ordination of our colleague Sabinus, that by the suffrage of the entire brotherhood, and by the judgment of the bishops who had assembled in their presence, the episcopate was conferred and hands laid on him.
text_raw: Accordingly, as regards the divine observance and apostolic practice, you must diligently keep and practice what is also observed among us and in almost all the provinces, that for celebrating ordination properly, whatsoever bishops of the same province live nearest should come together with the people for whom a pastor is being appointed, and the bishop should be chosen in the presence of the people, who most fully know the life of each one, which we also have seen done among us at the ordination of our colleague Sabinus, that by the suffrage of the entire brotherhood, and by the judgment of the bishops who had assembled in their presence, the episcopate was conferred and hands laid on him.

text: 15 Cyprian calls this custom a divine tradition and an apostolic observance, and affirms that it is observed in almost all the provinces.
text_raw: 15 Cyprian calls this custom a divine tradition and an apostolic observance, and affirms that it is observed in almost all the provinces.

text: Since, therefore, neither ordination nor confirmation was sought from a bishop of Rome in the greater part of the world in the Latin and Greek churches, it is sufficiently apparent that the churches did not then accord superiority and domination to the bishop of Rome.
text_raw: Since, therefore, neither ordination nor confirmation was sought from a bishop of Rome in the greater part of the world in the Latin and Greek churches, it is sufficiently apparent that the churches did not then accord superiority and domination to the bishop of Rome.

text: 16 Such superiority is impossible.
text_raw: 16 Such superiority is impossible.

text: For it is impossible for one bishop to be the overseer of the churches of the whole world, or for churches situated in the most distant lands to seek ordination [for all their ministers] from one.
text_raw: For it is impossible for one bishop to be the overseer of the churches of the whole world, or for churches situated in the most distant lands to seek ordination [for all their ministers] from one.

text: For it is manifest that the kingdom of Christ is scattered throughout the whole world; and to-day there are many churches in the East which do not seek ordination or confirmation from the Roman bishop [which have ministers ordained neither by the Pope nor his bishops].
text_raw: For it is manifest that the kingdom of Christ is scattered throughout the whole world; and to-day there are many churches in the East which do not seek ordination or confirmation from the Roman bishop [which have ministers ordained neither by the Pope nor his bishops].

text: Therefore, since such superiority [which the Pope, contrary to all Scripture, arrogates to himself] is impossible, and the churches in the greater part of the world have not acknowledged [nor made use of] it, it is sufficiently apparent that it was not instituted [by Christ, and does not spring from divine law].
text_raw: Therefore, since such superiority [which the Pope, contrary to all Scripture, arrogates to himself] is impossible, and the churches in the greater part of the world have not acknowledged [nor made use of] it, it is sufficiently apparent that it was not instituted [by Christ, and does not spring from divine law].

text: 17 VIII.
text_raw: 17 VIII.

text: Many ancient synods have been proclaimed and held in which the bishop of Rome did not preside; as that of Nice and most others.
text_raw: Many ancient synods have been proclaimed and held in which the bishop of Rome did not preside; as that of Nice and most others.

text: This, too, testifies that the Church did not then acknowledge the primacy or superiority of the bishop of Rome.
text_raw: This, too, testifies that the Church did not then acknowledge the primacy or superiority of the bishop of Rome.

text: 18 IX.
text_raw: 18 IX.

text: Jerome says:
text_raw: Jerome says:

text: If the question is concerning authority, the world is greater than the city.
text_raw: If the question is concerning authority, the world is greater than the city.

text: Wherever there has been a bishop, whether at Rome, or Eugubium, or Constantinople, or Rhegium, or Alexandria, he is of the same dignity and priesthood.
text_raw: Wherever there has been a bishop, whether at Rome, or Eugubium, or Constantinople, or Rhegium, or Alexandria, he is of the same dignity and priesthood.

text: Gregory, writing to the patriarch at Alexandria, forbids that he be called universal bishop.
text_raw: Gregory, writing to the patriarch at Alexandria, forbids that he be called universal bishop.

text: And in the Records he says that in the Council of Chalcedon the primacy was offered to the bishop of Rome, but was not accepted.
text_raw: And in the Records he says that in the Council of Chalcedon the primacy was offered to the bishop of Rome, but was not accepted.

text: 20 XI.
text_raw: 20 XI.

text: Lastly, how can the Pope be over the entire Church by divine right when the Church has the election, and the custom gradually prevailed that bishops of Rome were confirmed by the emperors?
text_raw: Lastly, how can the Pope be over the entire Church by divine right when the Church has the election, and the custom gradually prevailed that bishops of Rome were confirmed by the emperors?

text: 21 Also, when for a long time there had been contests concerning the primacy between the bishops of Rome and Constantinople, the Emperor Phocas finally determined that the primacy should be assigned to the bishop of Rome.
text_raw: 21 Also, when for a long time there had been contests concerning the primacy between the bishops of Rome and Constantinople, the Emperor Phocas finally determined that the primacy should be assigned to the bishop of Rome.

text: But if the ancient Church had acknowledged the primacy of the Roman Pontiff, this contention could not have occurred, neither would there have been need of the decree of the emperor.
text_raw: But if the ancient Church had acknowledged the primacy of the Roman Pontiff, this contention could not have occurred, neither would there have been need of the decree of the emperor.

text: For formerly the people elected pastors and bishops.

text: But he is a recent and fictitious author, whoever he may be [this book of Dionysius is a new fiction under a false title], just as the writings of Clement also are spurious [have a false title and have been manufactured by a wicked scoundrel long after Clement].

text: 74 It is certain that the common jurisdiction of excommunicating those guilty of manifest crimes belongs to all pastors.
text_raw: 74 It is certain that the common jurisdiction of excommunicating those guilty of manifest crimes belongs to all pastors.

text: This they have tyrannically transferred to themselves alone, and have applied it to the acquisition of gain.
text_raw: This they have tyrannically transferred to themselves alone, and have applied it to the acquisition of gain.

text: For it is certain that the officials, as they are called employed a license not to be tolerated and either on account of avarice or because of other wanton desires tormented men and excommunicated them without any due process of law.
text_raw: For it is certain that the officials, as they are called employed a license not to be tolerated and either on account of avarice or because of other wanton desires tormented men and excommunicated them without any due process of law.

text: But what tyranny is it for the officials in the states to have arbitrary power to condemn and excommunicate men without due process of law!
text_raw: But what tyranny is it for the officials in the states to have arbitrary power to condemn and excommunicate men without due process of law!

text: 75 And in what kind of affairs did they abuse this power?
text_raw: 75 And in what kind of affairs did they abuse this power?

text: Indeed, not in punishing true offenses, but in regard to the violation of fasts or festivals, or like trifles!
text_raw: Indeed, not in punishing true offenses, but in regard to the violation of fasts or festivals, or like trifles!

text: Only, they sometimes punished adulteries; and in this matter they often vexed [abused and defamed] innocent and honorable men.

text: Besides, since this is a most grievous offense, nobody certainly is to be condemned without due process of law.
text_raw: Besides, since this is a most grievous offense, nobody certainly is to be condemned without due process of law.

text: 76 Since, therefore, bishops have tyrannically transferred this jurisdiction to themselves alone, and have basely abused it, there is no need, because of this jurisdiction, to obey bishops.

text: But since there are just reasons why we do not obey, it is right also to restore this jurisdiction to godly pastors [to whom, by Christ’s command, it belongs], and to see to it that it is legitimately exercised for the reformation of morals and the glory of God.

text: 77 There remains the jurisdiction in those cases which, according to canonical law, pertain to the ecclesiastical court, as they call it, and especially in cases of matrimony.

text: This, too, the bishops have only by human right, and that, not a very old one, as appears from the Codex and Novellae of Justinian that decisions concerning marriage at that time belonged to the magistrates.

text: Therefore, also on account of this jurisdiction it is not necessary to obey bishops.
text_raw: Therefore, also on account of this jurisdiction it is not necessary to obey bishops.

text: 78 And, indeed, since they have framed certain unjust laws concerning marriages, and observe them in their courts, there is need also for this reason to establish other courts.

text: For the traditions concerning spiritual relationship [the prohibition of marriage between sponsors] are unjust.

text: Unjust also is the tradition which forbids an innocent person to marry after divorce.
text_raw: Unjust also is the tradition which forbids an innocent person to marry after divorce.

text: Unjust also is the law which in general approves all clandestine and underhanded betrothals in violation of the right of parents.

text: Unjust also is the law concerning the celibacy of priests.
text_raw: Unjust also is the law concerning the celibacy of priests.

text: There are also other snares of consciences in their laws, to recite all of which is of no profit.

text: It is sufficient to have recited this, that there are many unjust laws of the Pope concerning matrimonial subjects on account of which the magistrates ought to establish other courts.
